docs.title: 1. What Is Bluetooth?
docs.text:
Bluetooth is a short-range wireless communication technology used to exchange data between devices such as:

  • Phones 📱
  • Laptops 💻
  • Headphones 🎧
  • Keyboards & mice ⌨️
  • Smartwatches ⌚
  • IoT devices 🌐

Key idea:

Bluetooth connects devices directly, without cables, usually within 10–100 meters, using very low power.

docs.title: 2. Why Bluetooth Exists (Compared to Other Wireless Tech)
docs.text:
Technology Range Power Usage Typical Use Bluetooth Short Very low Headphones, keyboards Wi-Fi Medium High Internet, file transfer NFC Very short (cm) Extremely low Payments, pairing USB Cable N/A Fast, stable connection

👉 Bluetooth is optimized for:

  • Convenience
  • Low power
  • Simple device-to-device communication

docs.title: 3. Bluetooth Works on Radio Waves
docs.text:
Bluetooth uses the 2.4 GHz ISM band, the same frequency range as:

  • Wi-Fi
  • Microwaves
  • Some wireless keyboards

To avoid interference, Bluetooth uses:

docs.title: 🔁 Frequency Hopping
docs.text:
• Rapidly switches between 79 channels
  • Up to 1600 hops per second

This makes Bluetooth:

  • More reliable
  • Resistant to interference

docs.title: 4. Classic Bluetooth vs Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE)
docs.text: This is one of the most important beginner concepts.

docs.title: 4.1 Classic Bluetooth (BR/EDR)
docs.text:
Used for:

  • Audio streaming 🎧
  • Car systems 🚗
  • File transfer (older use)

Characteristics:

  • Continuous connection
  • Higher power usage
  • Higher data rate

Examples:

  • Bluetooth headphones
  • Bluetooth speakers

docs.title: 4.2 Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE)
docs.text:
Used for:

  • Fitness trackers
  • Smart home devices
  • Sensors
  • Beacons

Characteristics:

  • Extremely low power
  • Short data bursts
  • Can run for months or years on a coin battery

Examples:

  • Apple AirTag
  • Smart thermometers
  • Heart rate monitors

👉 Modern Bluetooth mostly means BLE

docs.title: 5. Bluetooth Versions (What the Numbers Mean)
docs.text:
Version Key Improvement Bluetooth 4.0 Introduced BLE Bluetooth 4.2 Better privacy, IPv6 Bluetooth 5.0 Longer range, higher speed Bluetooth 5.2 LE Audio, multi-stream Bluetooth 5.3+ Power & stability improvements

💡 Important:

  • Higher version ≠ faster device
  • Devices fall back to lowest common version

docs.title: 6.1 Central
docs.text:
• Initiates connection
  • Controls communication

Examples:

  • Phone
  • Laptop
  • Tablet

docs.title: 6.2 Peripheral
docs.text:
• Advertises itself
  • Waits to be connected

Examples:

  • Headphones
  • Smartwatch
  • Sensor

📱 Your phone is usually the Central

🎧 Your devices are usually Peripherals

docs.title: Pairing
docs.text:
• Exchange security keys
  • Happens once (usually)
  • Builds trust

docs.title: Connecting
docs.text:
• Actual data communication
  • Happens every time you use the device

Example:

Pair your headphones once → connect automatically later

docs.title: 8. Bluetooth Profiles (Classic Bluetooth)
docs.text:
Profiles define what Bluetooth is used for.

Profile Purpose A2DP Stereo audio HFP Hands-free calling HID Keyboard / mouse AVRCP Media control

👉 Devices must support the same profile to work together.

docs.title: 9. BLE Services, Characteristics (Core Concept)
docs.text: BLE uses a structured data model:

docs.title: GATT Hierarchy
docs.text:
Device
 └── Service (e.g. Heart Rate)
      └── Characteristic (e.g. Heart Rate Value)
  • Service = function group
  • Characteristic = actual data value
  • Characteristics can be:
    • Read
    • Write
    • Notify

Example:

  • Smart thermometer
    • Service: Temperature
    • Characteristic: Current temperature

docs.title: 10. Bluetooth Security (Beginner Level)
docs.text:
Bluetooth security includes:

  • Device authentication
  • Encryption
  • Permission control

docs.title: Pairing Methods
docs.text:
• PIN / Passkey
  • Numeric comparison
  • Just Works (less secure)

BLE adds:

  • Device privacy (random MAC addresses)
  • Encrypted characteristics

💡 For beginners:

  • Modern Bluetooth is reasonably secure
  • Avoid pairing with unknown devices in public

docs.title: Everyday
docs.text:
• Headphones 🎧
  • Car audio 🚗
  • Keyboard & mouse ⌨️

docs.title: Smart Devices
docs.text:
• Fitness bands
  • Smart bulbs
  • Smart locks

docs.title: Development / Engineering
docs.text:
• IoT devices
  • Sensors
  • Proximity beacons

docs.title: 12. Bluetooth Limitations (Be Honest)
docs.text:
Bluetooth is not perfect:

❌ Slower than Wi-Fi

❌ Limited range

❌ Can suffer interference

❌ Not ideal for large file transfer

Use it where:

  • Power efficiency matters
  • Data size is small
  • Convenience is key

docs.title: 13. How Beginners Should Learn Bluetooth (Suggested Path)
docs.text:
1. User perspective
    • Pairing
    • Troubleshooting
  2. Concepts
    • Classic vs BLE
    • Central / Peripheral
  3. Practical tools
    • Bluetooth settings
    • BLE scanner apps
  4. Advanced (optional)
    • GATT services
    • BLE development

docs.title: 14. Summary
docs.text: Bluetooth is a low-power, short-range wireless technology designed for simple, convenient device communication. Modern Bluetooth is dominated by Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE), which uses a central–peripheral model and a service-based data structure. Understanding pairing, roles, and basic BLE concepts is enough for most beginners to confidently use and even start developing Bluetooth-based systems.

docs.title: 1. What Is a Network Cable?
docs.text:
A network cable is a physical wire used to connect devices so they can communicate and share data.

Common examples:

  • Computer ↔ Router
  • Router ↔ Switch
  • PC ↔ PC (older setups)
  • NAS / Printer / IP Camera ↔ Network

In most homes and offices, when people say “network cable”, they mean an Ethernet cable.

docs.title: 2. Why Do We Still Need Network Cables?
docs.text:
Even with Wi-Fi everywhere, network cables are still important because they are:

  • Faster – higher and more stable speeds
  • More reliable – no wireless interference
  • Lower latency – great for gaming, servers, and streaming
  • More secure – physical access required

That’s why desktops, servers, switches, and access points usually use cables.

docs.title: 3. The Most Common Type: Ethernet Cable
3.1 Twisted Pair Cable
docs.text:
Almost all Ethernet cables today are twisted pair cables.

Inside the cable:

  • 8 copper wires
  • Twisted into 4 pairs
  • Twisting reduces electromagnetic interference

These cables usually end with an RJ45 connector.

docs.title: 4. Ethernet Cable Categories (Cat)
docs.text:
You’ll often see names like Cat5e, Cat6, etc. “Cat” means Category.

Category Max Speed Max Distance Common Use Cat5e 1 Gbps 100 m Home, office (still very common) Cat6 1 Gbps (10 Gbps short) 100 m (55 m @ 10G) Better shielding, newer installs Cat6a 10 Gbps 100 m Data centers, prosumer setups Cat7 10 Gbps 100 m Shielded, less common Cat8 25–40 Gbps 30 m Data centers only

Beginner tip:

👉 For most people, Cat5e or Cat6 is more than enough.

docs.title: 5. Shielding Types (UTP, STP, FTP)
docs.text:
Ethernet cables may or may not have shielding.

  • UTP (Unshielded Twisted Pair)
    • Most common
    • Cheap and flexible
    • Perfect for home use
  • STP / FTP (Shielded)
    • Extra metal shielding
    • Better against interference
    • Thicker, harder to install
    • Needs proper grounding

Rule of thumb: 🏠 Home → UTP

🏭 Factory / noisy environment → Shielded

docs.title: 6. RJ45 Connector
docs.text:
The plastic plug at the end of an Ethernet cable is called RJ45.

  • 8 pins
  • Clicks into place
  • Used by Ethernet ports on:
    • Routers
    • Switches
    • PCs
    • NAS devices

You’ll usually see tiny LEDs near the port:

  • Blinking = data activity
  • Color may indicate speed (device-dependent)

docs.title: Straight-Through Cable
docs.text:
• Same wiring order on both ends
  • Used for:
    • PC ↔ Router
    • Router ↔ Switch

docs.title: Crossover Cable
docs.text:
• Different wiring on each end
  • Used for:
    • PC ↔ PC (old hardware)

💡 Good news: Modern devices support Auto MDI-X, so you almost never need to care anymore.

docs.title: * 8. Ethernet Cable vs Other Network Cables
Ethernet vs Fiber
docs.text:
• Ethernet (copper)
    • Cheap, easy
    • Shorter distance
  • Fiber optic cable
    • Uses light, not electricity
    • Very long distance
    • Very fast
    • More expensive

docs.title: Ethernet vs Coaxial
docs.text:
• Coaxial is used for:
    • Cable TV
    • Cable modem (DOCSIS)
  • Ethernet is used after the modem inside your network

docs.title: 9. How to Choose the Right Network Cable
docs.text:
For most beginners:

  • ✅ Cat6 UTP
  • ✅ Length under 30 meters
  • ✅ Factory-made (not hand-crimped)
  • ✅ Known brand

Avoid:

  • Ultra-cheap “flat” cables for long runs
  • Cat7/Cat8 marketing hype for home use

docs.title: 10. Common Mistakes to Avoid
docs.text:
• Bending cables too sharply
  • Running Ethernet parallel to power cables
  • Using outdoor cables indoors (or vice versa)
  • Buying Cat8 for a 1 Gbps router 😄

docs.title: 11. Quick Summary
docs.text:
• Network cables connect devices physically
  • Ethernet cables are the most common
  • Cat5e / Cat6 are perfect for beginners
  • Wired networks are faster and more stable than Wi-Fi
  • You don’t need expensive cables for normal use

docs.title: 🖥️ 1. Quick Overview
docs.text: The BenQ PD2705U is a 27-inch 4K (3840×2160) IPS professional monitor designed for creators, designers, photographers and productivity users. It blends accurate color, ergonomic flexibility, and modern connectivity — making it ideal for creative workflows and everyday computing alike.(BenQ)

docs.title: 📺 Screen & Image Quality
docs.text:
• Display Size: 27 inches (diagonal)(BenQ)
  • Panel Type: IPS (wide viewing angles with good color accuracy)(BenQ)
  • Resolution: 3840 × 2160 (4K UHD) — very sharp for detailed work and text.(BenQ)
  • Aspect Ratio: 16:9 (standard widescreen).(BenQ)
  • Color Depth: ~1.07 billion colors (10-bit).(BenQ)
  • Pixel Density: ~163 PPI (crisp text and fine detail).(BenQ)

docs.title: 🌈 Brightness & Color
docs.text:
• Typical Brightness: 250 nits (standard content).(BenQ)
  • Peak HDR Brightness: 350 nits (HDR10).(BenQ)
  • High Dynamic Range: HDR10 support — wider dynamic range for compatible media.(BenQ)
  • Color Gamut: 99% sRGB + 99% Rec.709 — great for design, web, video editing in standard color spaces.(BenQ)
  • Contrast Ratio: ~1200:1 (good black & white differentiation).(BenQ)

docs.title: ⚡ Performance
docs.text:
• Refresh Rate: 60 Hz (standard PC/display).(BenQ)
  • Response Time: ~5 ms (fine for design and productivity, casual video).(BenQ)
  • Viewing Angles: 178°/178° (minimal shift from angles).(BenQ)

docs.title: 🔌 3. Connectivity & Hub Features
docs.text:
The PD2705U includes useful ports that help simplify your setup:(BenQ)

  • 1 × HDMI 2.0 — standard video input.(BenQ)
  • 1 × DisplayPort 1.4 — higher bandwidth for 4K content.(BenQ)
  • USB-C with Power Delivery (65 W) — video, data, and laptop charging in one cable.(BenQ)
  • USB Hub: multiple USB-A/USB-B downstream ports for keyboards, drives, etc.(BenQ)
  • Headphone Jack for audio output.(BenQ)
  • All-in-One USB-C connection integrates display + hub + power with one cable.(BenQ)

docs.title: * 🎨 4. Professional & Creative Features
docs.text: This monitor isn’t just hardware — it’s built for workflow and color precision:(BenQ)

docs.title: 🛠 Color & Modes
docs.text:
• Factory Calibrated: Accurate color out of the box.(BenQ)
  • Delta-E ≤ 3 average: Low color deviation.(BenQ)
  • Color Presets: Rec.709, sRGB, HDR, M-Book (for laptops/Mac), CAD/CAM, Animation, Darkroom, DICOM, Low Blue Light and custom.(BenQ)
  • Pantone & CalMAN Verified: Third-party color validation.(BenQ)

docs.title: 🔄 Productivity Helpers
docs.text:
• KVM Switch: Control two computers with one keyboard/mouse.(BenQ)
  • Picture-in-Picture (PIP) / Picture-by-Picture (PBP): Work with multiple sources.(BenQ)
  • Auto Pivot: Screen rotates between landscape/portrait automatically.(BenQ)
  • Hotkey Puck G2: Quick shortcut wheel for switching modes, adjusting settings, and more.(BenQ)
  • Display Pilot / Palette Master Software: Software to manage color modes and display layout.(BenQ)

docs.title: * 👁 Eye Comfort & Build
docs.text:
• Eye-Care: Flicker-free + Low Blue Light to reduce fatigue during long sessions.(BenQ)
  • Ergonomics: Height, tilt, swivel and pivot adjustable.(BenQ)
  • Matte Anti-Glare Coating: Reduces reflections.(BenQ)
  • VESA Mount (100 × 100 mm): For wall or arm mounting.(BenQ)

docs.title: * 🧰 5. Who Is This Monitor For?
docs.text:
Best suited for:

  • Graphic designers, photo/videographers who need accurate colors
  • Professionals working with sRGB/Rec.709 content
  • Multitaskers who benefit from USB-C + power delivery workflows
  • Anyone who prefers ergonomic adjustability and productivity features

Not ideal if:

  • You prioritize very high brightness for HDR video — peak is ~350 nits (good, not extreme).(BenQ)
  • You need a high refresh rate (e.g., competitive gaming) — it’s 60 Hz.(BenQ)

docs.title: * 🧠 Summary
docs.text:
Pros

  • Excellent color accuracy & industry certification.(BenQ)
  • USB-C with power delivery simplifies desk setup.(BenQ)
  • Great ergonomic and productivity features.(BenQ)
  • Good for professional creative work and general use.(BenQ)

Cons

  • Brightness not as high as some HDR-focused monitors.(BenQ)
  • Not designed for high-frame games (60 Hz only).(BenQ)

docs.title: Kobo Clare 2E Setup
docs.text: This guide provides a comprehensive walkthrough for setting up and optimizing your Kobo Clara 2E, specifically focusing on bypassing regional restrictions, enabling developer features, and installing essential third-party software.

docs.title: 1. Initial Setup & Account Bypass
docs.text: Because the Kobo Store cannot process purchases in certain countries (e.g., China), you can use a SQL injection to bypass the mandatory login.

docs.title: Bypass Steps:
docs.text:
1. Factory Reset: Go to More > Settings > Device Information > Advanced > Factory Reset.

  2. Skip Wi-Fi: On the welcome screen, select "Don't have a Wi-Fi network?".

  3. Database Modification:

    • Connect the Kobo to your PC via USB.

    • Open the .kobo/KoboReader.sqlite file using an SQLite editor. 

      $ sqlite3 .kobo/KoboReader.sqlite

    • Execute the following command:

      sqlite> INSERT INTO user(UserID, UserKey) VALUES ('1', '');
sqlite> .exit

  4. Restart: Eject and reboot. The "Discover" button will appear, and the account will show as logged in (with an empty username).

docs.title: Developer Mode
docs.text:
• Enable: Tap the Search icon and type devmodeon.
  • Effect: New games and experimental features will appear under More > Beta Features.

docs.title: Configuration File (Kobo eReader.conf)
docs.text:
Located at: KOBOeReader/.kobo/Kobo/Kobo eReader.conf. Add these lines to enable specific features:

[FeatureSettings]
# Prevent the device from scanning hidden system folders for books
ExcludeSyncFolders=(\\.(?!kobo|adobe).+|([^.][^/]*/)+\\..+)
# Enable the hidden "Export Highlights" menu option
ExportHighlights=true

docs.title: File Management & Conversion
docs.text:
• kepubify: Converts standard EPUBs to Kobo-optimized EPUBs (Kepub) for faster performance.
  • Send to Kobo: Wireless file transfer. Note: Filenames must not contain Chinese characters.

docs.title: Third-Party Apps
docs.text:
• NickelMenu - Adds custom shortcuts to the main menu.
  • NickelClock - Displays a clock in the header/footer while reading.
  • KOReader - A powerful alternative document viewer (highly recommended for PDFs).
  • KoboCloud - Syncs books from Dropbox, Google Drive, or pCloud.
  • Plato

docs.title: 4. Custom NickelMenu Configuration
docs.text:
To customize your menu, edit .adds/nm/config. Below is a recommended setup for quick access to system toggles and games:

Category Command Examples System Reboot, Dark Mode Toggle, Screenshot Toggle Tools Web Browser, Reading Life Statistics Games Sketch Pad, Sudoku, Unblock It (Hua Rong Dao) Custom menu_item :main :Send to Kobo :nickel_browser :modal :https://send.djazz.se 
# ==============================================================================
# NICKELMENU CONFIGURATION
# Location: KOBOeReader/.adds/nm/config
# ==============================================================================

# --- [ MAIN MENU: SYSTEM & POWER ] ---
# Quickly reboot the device
menu_item :main :Reboot 重启 :power :reboot

# --- [ MAIN MENU: CONNECTIVITY & TOOLS ] ---
# Wireless file transfer service (Note: avoid Chinese characters in filenames)

# Open the built-in web browser
menu_item :main :Browser 浏览器 :nickel_browser :modal

# View reading statistics and awards
menu_item :main :Reading Life 阅读统计 :nickel_open :reading_life:reading_life

# --- [ MAIN MENU: SETTINGS TOGGLES ] ---
# Toggle high-contrast dark mode
menu_item :main :Dark Mode 夜间模式 :nickel_setting :toggle :dark_mode

# Toggle the ability to take screenshots by pressing the power button
menu_item :main :Screenshots 截图 :nickel_setting :toggle :screenshots

# --- [ MAIN MENU: ANNOTATION SYNC ] ---
# Connects to WiFi and runs a script to export all highlights and notes
menu_item :main    :Sync Annotations 导出全部注释    :nickel_wifi     :autoconnect
  chain_success                         :cmd_spawn       :quiet:/mnt/onboard/.adds/notes/notes.sh
  chain_success                         :dbg_toast       :Syncing Notes 导出成功
  chain_failure                         :dbg_toast       :Syncing Notes 导出失败

# --- [ MAIN MENU: EXTRAS & GAMES ] ---
# Access hidden beta features and games
menu_item :main :Sketch Pad 涂鸦板 :nickel_extras :sketch_pad
menu_item :main :Sudoku 数独 :nickel_extras :sudoku
menu_item :main :Unblock It 华容道 :nickel_extras :unblock_it

# --- [ READER MENU: IN-BOOK CONTROLS ] ---
# These items appear in the menu while you are actively reading a book
menu_item :reader :Screenshots 截图 :nickel_setting :toggle :screenshots
menu_item :reader :Dark Mode 夜间模式 :nickel_setting :toggle :dark_mode

docs.title: 1. What Is Kobo Clara 2E?
docs.text:
The Kobo Clara 2E is a compact e-ink e-reader designed for comfortable, distraction-free reading. It is made by Rakuten Kobo, a company well known for open, reader-friendly devices.

The “2E” stands for “2nd Edition, Eco-friendly”, highlighting its use of recycled materials and improved hardware over the original Clara.

docs.title: 2. Why Choose an E-Ink Reader?
docs.text: Before diving into the device itself, it helps to understand why people use e-readers.

docs.title: E-Ink vs Tablets / Phones
docs.text:
Feature E-Ink Reader Phone / Tablet Eye comfort Very high Lower (backlit LCD) Battery life Weeks Hours / days Distractions None Notifications, apps Outdoor reading Excellent Poor in sunlight

Kobo Clara 2E feels closer to reading real paper than using a screen.

docs.title: 3. Key Specifications (Beginner View)
docs.text:
• Screen:
    • 6-inch E-Ink Carta 1200
    • 300 PPI (very sharp text)
  • Front Light:
    • Adjustable brightness
    • Adjustable color temperature (warm light at night)
  • Storage:
    • 16 GB (thousands of books)
  • Waterproof:
    • IPX8 (safe for bath, pool, rain)
  • Battery Life:
    • Up to several weeks per charge
  • Charging Port:
    • USB-C

docs.title: Buttons & Ports
docs.text:
• Power button: On the back
  • USB-C port: Bottom edge
  • Touch screen: Used for all navigation

There are no page-turn buttons—you swipe or tap the screen.

docs.title: Step 1: Power On
docs.text: Hold the back power button for a few seconds.

docs.title: Step 2: Choose Language & Wi-Fi
docs.text: Select your language and connect to Wi-Fi.

docs.title: Step 3: Sign in to Kobo Account
docs.text:
You can:

  • Create a new Kobo account
  • Sign in with an existing one

This account is used for syncing books and reading progress.

docs.title: Method 1: Kobo Store (Built-in)
docs.text:
• Access directly from the device
  • Buy or download free books
  • Books sync automatically

docs.title: Method 2: Public Domain / Free Books
docs.text:
You can add:

  • Project Gutenberg books
  • DRM-free EPUB files

docs.title: Method 3: USB Transfer (Local Files)
docs.text:
1. Connect Kobo to your computer
  2. Copy EPUB / PDF / MOBI (limited) files
  3. Safely eject the device

Kobo is especially friendly to EPUB, unlike Kindle.

docs.title: 7. Supported File Formats
docs.text:
Common formats include:

  • EPUB (best choice)
  • EPUB3
  • PDF
  • TXT
  • HTML
  • CBZ / CBR (comics)

📌 Tip: EPUB offers the best font resizing and layout control.

docs.title: Page Turning
docs.text:
• Tap right side → next page
  • Tap left side → previous page
  • Swipe left/right

docs.title: Adjusting Text
docs.text:
While reading, tap the center:

  • Font size
  • Font type
  • Line spacing
  • Margins

docs.title: Night Reading
docs.text:
Enable ComfortLight PRO:

  • Reduce blue light
  • Warm amber tone for night use

docs.title: 9. Annotations & Highlights
docs.text:
You can:

  • Long-press text to highlight
  • Add notes
  • View all highlights later

This is useful for:

  • Studying
  • Language learning
  • Academic reading

docs.title: 10. Battery & Charging Tips
docs.text:
• Charge with USB-C
  • A full charge can last weeks
  • Turn off Wi-Fi when not syncing to save power

E-ink screens consume power only when changing pages.

docs.title: 11. Waterproof Use
docs.text:
Kobo Clara 2E is:

  • Safe for bath reading
  • Safe near pools
  • Not designed for salt water or soap immersion

Always dry the USB-C port before charging.

docs.title: 12. Kobo vs Kindle (Quick Comparison)
docs.text:
Feature Kobo Clara 2E Kindle (basic) EPUB support Yes No OverDrive (library) Yes Limited UI openness High Closed Ads No Sometimes USB-C Yes Depends on model

Kobo is often preferred by users who value file freedom and local libraries.

docs.title: 13. Who Is Kobo Clara 2E For?
docs.text:
Ideal if you:

  • Read novels or non-fiction regularly
  • Want a small, portable e-reader
  • Prefer EPUB and DRM-free books
  • Care about eye comfort and battery life

Less ideal if you:

  • Read large PDFs or textbooks
  • Need color (comics, magazines)

docs.title: 14. Final Thoughts
docs.text:
Kobo Clara 2E is a:

  • Simple
  • Comfortable
  • Open
  • Eco-friendly

e-reader that focuses on reading first, without distractions.

docs.title: 1. What Is DisplayPort?
docs.text:
DisplayPort (DP) is a digital display interface used to connect a computer to:

  • Monitors 🖥️
  • TVs 📺 (less common)
  • Docking stations
  • Projectors

It carries both video and audio over a single cable.

Think of DisplayPort as:

HDMI’s more “PC-focused”, more powerful cousin

docs.title: 2. Where Do You See DisplayPort?
docs.text:
Common places you’ll find DP:

  • Desktop graphics cards (very common)
  • PC monitors
  • Laptops (often Mini DP or USB-C DP)
  • Docking stations

Typical DP logo:

DP

or a D-shaped connector with one corner cut

docs.title: 3. DisplayPort vs HDMI (Quick Intuition)
docs.text:
Feature DisplayPort HDMI Designed for PCs, monitors TVs, home media High refresh rate ✅ Very strong ⚠️ Limited (older versions) Daisy-chain monitors ✅ Yes ❌ No Audio support ✅ Yes ✅ Yes Free & open ✅ Mostly ❌ Licensing

Rule of thumb:

  • 🖥️ PC + Monitor → DisplayPort
  • 📺 TV / Console → HDMI

docs.title: 4. DisplayPort Versions (Simple Overview)
docs.text:
Version Max Capability (Typical) DP 1.2 4K @ 60Hz DP 1.4 4K @ 120Hz / 8K @ 60Hz (with compression) DP 2.0 / 2.1 8K+ high refresh (very high bandwidth)

👉 Most people today use DP 1.4, and that’s totally fine.

docs.title: 5. Why Gamers and Developers Love DisplayPort 🎮💻
① High Refresh Rates
docs.text:
DisplayPort handles:

  • 144Hz
  • 165Hz
  • 240Hz much more reliably than older HDMI.

docs.title: ② Adaptive Sync
docs.text:
Supports:

  • FreeSync
  • G-Sync (compatible)

This reduces:

  • Screen tearing
  • Stuttering

docs.title: ③ Multi-Stream Transport (MST)
docs.text:
One DP cable → multiple monitors

Example:

PC ── DP ── Monitor 1 ── DP ── Monitor 2

(Only works if monitors support MST.)

docs.title: Standard DisplayPort
docs.text:
• Large connector
  • Common on desktops & monitors

docs.title: Mini DisplayPort (Mini DP)
docs.text:
• Smaller
  • Seen on older laptops (MacBooks, ThinkPads)

docs.title: DisplayPort over USB-C
docs.text:
Modern laptops often output DP via USB-C

Look for:

  • Thunderbolt ⚡
  • DP Alt Mode

Same DisplayPort signal, just different plug.

docs.title: Common cables
docs.text:
• DP → DP (best choice)
  • Mini DP → DP
  • USB-C → DP

docs.title: Adapters
docs.text:
• DP → HDMI (works, but limited by HDMI)
  • HDMI → DP (⚠️ usually does NOT work unless active adapter)

👉 Direction matters!

docs.title: 8. Audio Over DisplayPort?
docs.text:
Yes ✅

DisplayPort can carry:

  • Stereo audio
  • Multi-channel audio

If your monitor has speakers or headphone output, DP can feed them.

docs.title: 9. Common Beginner Mistakes ❌
docs.text:
❌ Using HDMI cable and wondering why 144Hz doesn’t show

❌ Cheap DP cable causing black screen / flicker

❌ Plugging HDMI → DP adapter backward

❌ Forgetting to enable high refresh rate in OS settings

docs.title: 10. When Should You Choose DisplayPort?
docs.text:
Choose DisplayPort if:

  • You use a PC monitor
  • You want high refresh rates
  • You use multiple monitors
  • You care about smooth gaming or coding

Choose HDMI if:

  • You connect to a TV
  • You use consoles or media devices

docs.title: 11. TL;DR
docs.text:
• DisplayPort = modern PC display interface
  • Better than HDMI for:
    • High refresh rates
    • Multi-monitor setups
  • DP 1.4 is more than enough for most users
  • USB-C often carries DisplayPort signals

docs.title: 1. What Is Thunderbolt?
docs.text:
Thunderbolt is a high-speed hardware interface developed by Intel (in collaboration with Apple).

In simple terms, Thunderbolt is:

One cable that can carry data, video, and power at very high speed

It is commonly used for:

  • External SSDs
  • High-resolution monitors
  • Docking stations
  • eGPUs
  • Professional audio/video equipment

docs.title: 2. Why Does Thunderbolt Exist?
docs.text:
USB is great for everyday devices, but it has limits.

Thunderbolt was designed to solve problems like:

  • Moving huge files very fast
  • Connecting multiple high-resolution displays
  • Extending PCIe devices outside the computer
  • Replacing many cables with one cable

Think of Thunderbolt as:

“External PCIe + DisplayPort + USB combined”

docs.title: 3. Thunderbolt vs USB (Big Picture)
docs.text:
Feature USB Thunderbolt Typical Use General peripherals High-performance devices Speed Up to 40 Gbps (USB4) 40 Gbps Architecture Device-oriented PCIe-oriented Daisy-chain Limited Yes eGPU support No Yes Cost Low Higher

📌 Thunderbolt is more powerful, but not always necessary.

docs.title: Important Rule
docs.text:
All modern Thunderbolt uses the USB-C connector

But:

  • Not all USB-C ports support Thunderbolt
  • Not all USB-C cables support Thunderbolt

Look for the ⚡ lightning symbol near the port.

docs.title: 5. Thunderbolt Versions
docs.text:
Version Max Speed Notes Thunderbolt 1 10 Gbps Mini DisplayPort Thunderbolt 2 20 Gbps Mini DisplayPort Thunderbolt 3 40 Gbps USB-C Thunderbolt 4 40 Gbps Stricter requirements

📌 Thunderbolt 4 improves reliability, not raw speed.

docs.title: 6. What Runs Inside a Thunderbolt Cable?
docs.text:
Thunderbolt tunnels multiple protocols at once:

  • PCI Express (PCIe) → SSDs, eGPUs
  • DisplayPort → monitors
  • USB → backward compatibility
  • Power Delivery → charging

This is why Thunderbolt docks are so powerful.

docs.title: 7. Daisy-Chaining Devices
docs.text:
Thunderbolt supports daisy-chain:

Laptop ── Monitor ── SSD ── Dock
  • Up to 6 devices
  • One cable to the computer
  • Devices share total bandwidth

USB hubs ≠ Thunderbolt daisy-chain.

docs.title: 8. Thunderbolt and Displays
docs.text:
With Thunderbolt you can:

  • Drive multiple 4K monitors
  • Or one 5K / 8K monitor
  • Use a single cable for:
    • Video
    • Power
    • USB devices

This is common on Macs and high-end laptops.

docs.title: 9. Thunderbolt Power Delivery
docs.text:
Thunderbolt supports USB Power Delivery:

  • Up to 100 W (and more with USB-PD Extended)
  • Can charge laptops
  • One cable for:
    • Charging
    • Data
    • Display

This enables “one-cable desks”.

docs.title: 10. Thunderbolt vs USB4 (Common Confusion)
docs.text: USB4 is based on Thunderbolt 3 technology.

docs.title: Key differences:
docs.text:
USB4 Thunderbolt Optional features Mandatory features May skip PCIe Must support PCIe Certification looser Strict certification

📌 Thunderbolt guarantees performance; USB4 does not.

docs.title: 11. When Do You Actually Need Thunderbolt?
docs.text:
You need Thunderbolt if you use:

  • External NVMe SSDs at full speed
  • Multiple high-resolution monitors
  • eGPU
  • Professional A/V gear
  • High-end docking stations

You do NOT need Thunderbolt if you:

  • Just charge devices
  • Use keyboard/mouse
  • Copy small files
  • Use basic USB hubs

docs.title: 12. How to Check If Your Computer Supports Thunderbolt
docs.text:
1. Look for ⚡ symbol on the port
  2. Check system specs
  3. macOS:
    • System Information → Thunderbolt
  4. Linux:
    • boltctl list
  5. Windows:
    • Thunderbolt Control Center

docs.title: 13. Safety and Security
docs.text:
Thunderbolt exposes PCIe → powerful but risky.

Modern systems add:

  • Device authorization
  • DMA protection
  • IOMMU isolation

Always trust devices you connect.

docs.title: 14. Summary
docs.text:
• Thunderbolt = high-speed, multi-protocol interface
  • Uses USB-C connector
  • Much more powerful than typical USB
  • Supports PCIe, displays, power
  • Ideal for professional and high-performance setups

docs.title: 1. What Is USB?
docs.text:
USB stands for Universal Serial Bus.

In simple terms, USB is a standard way to connect devices to a computer so they can:

  • 🔌 Get power
  • 📁 Transfer data
  • 🎮 Communicate (keyboard input, mouse movement, etc.)

USB is everywhere: flash drives, keyboards, mice, phones, webcams, printers, development boards, and more.

docs.title: 2. What Problems Does USB Solve?
docs.text:
Before USB, computers had many different ports:

  • Serial ports
  • Parallel ports
  • PS/2 (keyboard/mouse)
  • Proprietary connectors

USB unified all of these by providing:

  • One common connector
  • Automatic device detection
  • Hot-plugging (plug/unplug without reboot)
  • Standard power delivery

docs.title: 3.1 Host and Device
docs.text:
USB works in a master–slave model:

  • Host: Controls the connection
    • Usually a PC, laptop, or smartphone
  • Device: Gets controlled
    • Keyboard, mouse, USB drive, phone, etc.

📌 Important:

Devices cannot talk directly to each other without a host.

docs.title: 3.2 USB Cable Has Two Ends
docs.text:
A USB cable is not symmetric (except USB-C):

  • Host side → connects to computer
  • Device side → connects to peripheral

This design enforces the host–device relationship.

docs.title: 4.1 USB Type-A
docs.text:
• Flat, rectangular
  • Found on PCs, chargers, hubs
  • Host side
[====]

docs.title: 4.2 USB Type-B
docs.text:
• Square with corners cut
  • Used by printers, scanners
  • Device side

docs.title: 4.3 USB Mini & Micro
docs.text:
• Older phones, cameras, development boards
  • Micro-USB was very common before USB-C

docs.title: 4.4 USB Type-C (Modern Standard)
docs.text:
• Reversible (no “wrong side”)
  • Can be host or device
  • Supports:
    • Data
    • Power
    • Video (DisplayPort / HDMI Alt Mode)

📌 USB-C is a connector, not a speed standard.

docs.title: 5. USB Versions (Speed Matters)
docs.text:
USB Version Max Speed Common Name USB 1.1 12 Mbps Very old USB 2.0 480 Mbps Still common USB 3.0 / 3.2 Gen 1 5 Gbps “SuperSpeed” USB 3.2 Gen 2 10 Gbps Faster USB4 40 Gbps High-end

📌 A USB-C cable may still run at USB 2.0 speed!

docs.title: 6. Power Delivery over USB
docs.text: USB doesn’t just carry data — it also provides power.

docs.title: 6.1 Basic Power
docs.text:
• USB 2.0: up to 2.5 W
  • USB 3.0: up to 4.5 W

Enough for:

  • Mouse
  • Keyboard
  • USB flash drive

docs.title: 6.2 USB Power Delivery (USB-PD)
docs.text:
Modern USB-C supports USB-PD:

  • Up to 240 W
  • Can power:
    • Laptops
    • Monitors
    • Docking stations

📌 Power is negotiated between devices.

docs.title: 7. How USB Communication Works (High Level)
docs.text:
When you plug in a USB device:

  1. Host detects a new device
  2. Device identifies itself (class, vendor, product)
  3. Host loads a driver
  4. Data transfer begins

This process is called enumeration.

docs.title: 8. USB Device Classes (Why Drivers Often “Just Work”)
docs.text:
Many USB devices follow standard USB classes:

Device USB Class Keyboard / Mouse HID Flash Drive Mass Storage Webcam Video Audio Interface Audio

Because of this:

  • No manual driver install needed
  • Plug and play works

docs.title: 9. USB Hubs
docs.text:
A USB hub:

  • Expands 1 USB port → many ports
  • Still has one host
PC ── Hub ── Mouse
        ├─ Keyboard
        ├─ Flash Drive

📌 All devices share bandwidth through the hub.

docs.title: ❓ USB-C vs USB 3.x
docs.text:
• USB-C = connector shape
  • USB 3.x / USB4 = speed & protocol

You can have:

  • USB-C + USB 2.0 (slow)
  • USB-A + USB 3.0 (fast)

docs.title: ❓ Charging Cable vs Data Cable
docs.text:
Some cheap cables:

  • Carry power only
  • No data wires inside

Always check cable specs if data transfer fails.

docs.title: 11. USB in Daily Life Examples
docs.text:
• Plugging a flash drive → Mass Storage
  • Phone charging → USB-PD
  • Keyboard input → HID
  • Webcam → USB Video Class

USB is the hidden infrastructure behind most peripherals.

docs.title: 12. Summary
docs.text:
• USB = Universal Serial Bus
  • One host controls many devices
  • Carries data + power
  • Connector ≠ speed
  • USB-C is modern, flexible, but confusing
  • Plug-and-play works thanks to USB classes

docs.title: 1. What Is HDMI?
docs.text:
HDMI stands for High-Definition Multimedia Interface.

It is a digital cable and standard used to transmit:

  • 📺 Video
  • 🔊 Audio

over a single cable, from one device to another.

In simple terms:

HDMI = one cable for picture + sound

docs.title: 2. Where Is HDMI Used?
docs.text:
HDMI is everywhere:

  • TVs 📺
  • Monitors 🖥️
  • Laptops 💻
  • Game consoles 🎮 (PS, Xbox, Switch)
  • Set-top boxes / TV boxes
  • Projectors

If it has a screen, it probably has HDMI.

docs.title: 3. What Does an HDMI Cable Carry?
docs.text:
An HDMI cable can carry:

  • High-resolution video (1080p, 4K, 8K)
  • Multi-channel audio (stereo, surround sound)
  • Control signals (CEC)
  • Copy protection data (HDCP)

All digitally — no quality loss like old VGA.

docs.title: 4. HDMI vs Old Display Cables
docs.text:
Cable Video Audio Digital VGA ✅ ❌ ❌ DVI ✅ ❌ (mostly) ✅ HDMI ✅ ✅ ✅

HDMI replaced most older connectors because it’s simple and universal.

docs.title: 5. HDMI Versions (What Actually Matters)
docs.text:
HDMI versions affect maximum resolution & refresh rate.

HDMI Version Typical Max HDMI 1.4 4K @ 30Hz HDMI 2.0 4K @ 60Hz HDMI 2.1 4K @ 120Hz / 8K

👉 Most TVs today support HDMI 2.0 or 2.1.

⚠️ Important:

The cable AND both devices must support the version.

docs.title: 6. HDMI Cable Types (This Confuses Beginners)
docs.text:
You’ll see labels like:

  • High Speed HDMI
  • Premium High Speed
  • Ultra High Speed

docs.title: Simple rule:
docs.text:
• 1080p / 4K 60Hz → High Speed HDMI
  • 4K 120Hz / 8K → Ultra High Speed HDMI

💡 Brand doesn’t matter much — certification does.

docs.title: Standard HDMI (Type A)
docs.text:
• Most common
  • TVs, monitors, consoles

docs.title: Mini HDMI (Type C)
docs.text: • Some cameras

docs.title: Micro HDMI (Type D)
docs.text:
• Small devices (action cameras)

All carry the same signal — just different sizes.

docs.title: 8. Audio Features (Why HDMI Is Great for TVs)
docs.text:
HDMI supports advanced audio formats:

  • Dolby Digital
  • DTS
  • Dolby Atmos (via HDMI 2.1 / eARC)

docs.title: ARC & eARC (TV users)
docs.text:
• ARC: TV sends audio back to soundbar
  • eARC: Higher quality, less compression

One HDMI cable can handle everything.

docs.title: 9. HDMI CEC (Hidden but Useful)
docs.text:
CEC lets devices control each other:

  • TV remote controls soundbar
  • Console turns TV on automatically

Names differ by brand:

  • Samsung: Anynet+
  • Sony: Bravia Sync
  • LG: Simplink

Same idea, different marketing.

docs.title: 10. Common Beginner Problems ❌
docs.text:
❌ 144Hz not available on monitor

→ HDMI version too old

❌ No sound on TV

→ Audio output not set correctly

❌ Screen flickering

→ Bad or too-long cable

❌ Adapter confusion

→ HDMI → DP ≠ DP → HDMI

docs.title: 11. HDMI vs DisplayPort (Quick Choice Guide)
docs.text:
Use Case Choose TV / Console HDMI PC + Monitor DisplayPort Home theater HDMI High-refresh gaming monitor DP (usually)

HDMI is consumer-electronics first.

docs.title: 12. When Should You Use HDMI?
docs.text:
Use HDMI if:

  • You connect to a TV
  • You use a game console
  • You want easy plug-and-play
  • You care about home audio features

docs.title: 13. TL;DR
docs.text:
• HDMI = universal audio + video cable
  • Perfect for TVs and home entertainment
  • HDMI 2.0 → 4K 60Hz
  • HDMI 2.1 → 4K 120Hz
  • Simple, reliable, everywhere

docs.title: 🖨️ 1) What It Is — Overview
docs.text: The HP Smart Tank 672 is an all-in-one wireless inkjet printer that lets you print, scan, and copy documents. It features a built-in wireless connection (Wi-Fi) and uses large refillable ink tanks (Smart Tank system) instead of standard cartridges. (support.hp.com)

docs.title: 🧰 Key Specs
docs.text:
• Functions: Print, Scan, Copy, Wireless (support.hp.com)
  • Print Speed: ~12 ppm (black), ~7 ppm (color) (ISO) (support.hp.com)
  • Print Quality: Up to 1200 x 1200 dpi (black); optimized color quality ~4800 x 1200 dpi (support.hp.com)
  • Paper Handling: Up to A4 size, ~150 sheets input (support.hp.com)
  • Scanner: Flatbed scanner up to A4 size (support.hp.com)
  • Connectivity: Wi-Fi (2.4/5 GHz), Wi-Fi Direct, USB (support.hp.com)

docs.title: 📦 2) Unboxing & Setup
docs.text: Start with the hardware setup before using your printer:

docs.title: 👇 Step-by-Step
docs.text:
1. Unpack the Printer Remove all packaging, tapes, and protective materials. Place the printer on a stable surface.
  2. Connect Power & Turn On Plug the power cable into the printer and wall outlet, then press the power button.
  3. Fill the Ink Tanks The Smart Tank has visible refillable ink tanks — fill them with the provided HP ink bottles. (Avoid overfilling.)
  4. Install Printheads / Remove Protective Clips Follow the instructions on the setup guide to install the printheads and remove all protective parts.
  5. Load Paper Put plain A4 paper into the input tray.
  6. Printhead Alignment After powering on, the printer will prompt for alignment — this ensures accurate print quality.

These steps are similar to the wider Smart Tank series; HP provides detailed setup guides on its official support site. (support.hp.com)

📺 Optional: You can also watch the official HP setup video covering the Smart Tank 670 series (which includes model 672). (YouTube)

docs.title: 📱 3) Install Software & Connect
docs.text: To use all features (especially wireless printing and scanning):

docs.title: 🔧 On Your Computer or Mobile
docs.text:
1. Download the HP Smart app From HP’s website or your device’s app store — this app guides you through setup and lets you print/scan from your phone or computer. (support.hp.com)
  2. Connect to Wi-Fi During setup, the app will help connect your printer to your Wi-Fi network. You can also use Wi-Fi Direct if you don’t want a router connection. (support.hp.com)
    1. 重置网络连接：首先按下 i 按钮5秒钟，然后同时按下Wi-Fi和 x 按钮5秒钟。
  3. Install Drivers (mostly for PCs) On a Windows or macOS system, install the recommended HP drivers when prompted by the setup tool.

⚠️ Tip: If Wi-Fi settings change and you need to reconnect the printer later, you may need to reset its network and re-run setup through HP Smart. (h30471.www3.hp.com)

docs.title: ✏️ Printing
docs.text:
• Open a document, photo, or web page, and choose Print.
  • Select the HP Smart Tank 672 as your printer.
  • Adjust settings (color, quality, paper size) before printing.

docs.title: 📄 Scanning
docs.text:
• Place your document face-down on the scanner glass.
  • Use the HP Smart app or your system’s scanning tool.
  • Save scans as JPEG or PDF.

docs.title: 📚 Copying
docs.text:
• Place the original on the scanner glass.
  • Press Copy on the printer UI or via the HP Smart app.

docs.title: 🛠️ 5) Common Tips & Troubleshooting
docs.text:
• Ink Levels: Check ink levels regularly — refill before running out.
  • Network: If the printer loses Wi-Fi, use the HP Smart app to reconnect. In some cases, you may need to reset the network settings. (h30471.www3.hp.com)
  • Driver Issues: Make sure the proper HP drivers are installed on your computer for best performance.

docs.title: ✅ Summary
docs.text: The HP Smart Tank 672 is a solid all-in-one printer solution for everyday printing, scanning, and copying with refillable ink tanks and wireless connectivity. After unpacking, filling ink, and connecting via the HP Smart app, you’ll be ready to print from your devices easily. (support.hp.com)

docs.title: Printers
docs.text:
This post documents the printers I own, what I know about them, and how I use and maintain them.

It also serves as a simple reference on common printer brands, basic printer concepts, and usage tips.

docs.title: 1. Introduction to Printers
docs.text:
A printer is a peripheral device that produces physical output (usually on paper) from digital data. Most consumer printers today fall into two major categories:

  • Inkjet printers — versatile, capable of printing photos and documents, generally lower upfront cost.
  • Laser printers — faster and more efficient for high-volume text printing, typically lower cost per page.

Modern home printers often support Wi-Fi, automatic duplex printing, mobile printing, and integrated ink tanks to reduce long-term consumable costs.

docs.title: 2. Printers I Own
docs.text: Purchase Date Brand Model Price Paid (CNY) 2024-11-23 EPSON L4266 1310.07 2023-07-12 HP Tank 672 1499

docs.title: EPSON L4266
docs.text:
The Epson L4266 is an ink-tank color inkjet printer known for its low cost per page and efficient ink usage. Key features include:

  • EcoTank design with refillable ink bottles
  • Duplex (double-sided) printing
  • Wi-Fi and mobile printing support
  • Good photo and document quality

It is suitable for home or small-office environments that require economical color printing.

docs.title: HP Tank 672
docs.text:
The HP Tank 672 is HP’s Smart Tank series device, similarly focused on low-cost, high-yield printing. Notable features:

  • Integrated refillable ink tank system
  • Reliable text quality and decent color output
  • Simple setup with HP Smart
  • Stable Wi-Fi performance

It is a practical option for users who print frequently and want predictable running costs.

docs.title: 4. Common Printer Brands
docs.text:
Below are some of the major brands in the consumer and office printer market:

  • EPSON – Strong in inkjet, EcoTank series, photo printing
  • HP – Popular home and office printers, Smart Tank and LaserJet series
  • Canon – Known for photo printers and balanced inkjet models
  • Brother – Often preferred for laser printers and office reliability
  • Pantum – Emerging budget-friendly laser printer brand
  • Ricoh / Kyocera – Common in enterprise environments

docs.title: General Usage
docs.text:
• Connect via Wi-Fi or USB depending on environment.
  • For mobile printing, use Epson iPrint or HP Smart.
  • Enable duplex printing when possible to save paper.

docs.title: Ink Refilling
docs.text:
• Always use original or high-quality compatible ink.
  • Refill slowly to avoid air bubbles in the ink tank.
  • Keep ink bottles tightly sealed when not in use.

docs.title: Print Quality Optimization
docs.text:
• Run nozzle cleaning if colors appear broken or faded.
  • Use the alignment tool to fix skewed text or lines.
  • For photos, choose high-quality photo paper and adjust print settings accordingly.

docs.title: Maintenance Tips
docs.text:
• Print something (even a single page) every 1–2 weeks to prevent ink drying.
  • Keep the printer in a cool, dry environment away from dust.
  • Avoid turning the printer on/off too frequently; this can waste ink on cleaning cycles.

docs.title: GL.iNet
docs.text:
Small Devices, Big Networking Power

GL.iNet (often written as GL.iNet / GL-iNet) is a networking company best known for its compact, open-source-friendly routers designed for developers, travelers, and privacy-conscious users.

Founded in 2014, GL.iNet focuses on building portable, customizable, and secure networking devices that go far beyond what typical consumer routers offer.

docs.title: What Does GL.iNet Do?
docs.text:
GL.iNet designs and sells:

  • Portable travel routers
  • Home and office routers
  • IoT gateways
  • Network security devices

Their products are widely used for:

  • Secure internet access while traveling
  • VPN routing (WireGuard / OpenVPN)
  • Network experiments and learning
  • Self-hosted services and homelabs
  • Bypassing complex or restricted networks (legally and responsibly)

docs.title: OpenWrt at the Core
docs.text:
One of GL.iNet’s biggest strengths is its deep integration with OpenWrt.

  • Most GL.iNet routers run customized OpenWrt
  • Users can install packages with opkg
  • Full access to SSH, firewall rules, and network configs
  • Easy switch between beginner-friendly UI and advanced OpenWrt features

This makes GL.iNet devices especially popular among:

  • Developers
  • Linux users
  • Network learners
  • DIY homelab enthusiasts

docs.title: 1. VPN-First Design
docs.text:
GL.iNet routers are built with VPN usage in mind:

  • One-click setup for WireGuard and OpenVPN
  • Act as VPN client or VPN server
  • Route selected devices through VPN only
  • Kill switch and DNS protection

docs.title: 2. Portable and Travel-Friendly
docs.text:
Many models are:

  • Pocket-sized
  • USB-powered
  • Lightweight
  • Easy to deploy in hotels, cafés, or dorms

Perfect for travelers who want:

  • A trusted Wi-Fi network
  • Consistent IP and DNS behavior
  • Better privacy on public Wi-Fi

docs.title: 3. Developer-Friendly
docs.text:
GL.iNet devices are ideal for learning and experimentation:

  • SSH access by default
  • Supports custom scripts and services
  • Can run lightweight servers (AdGuard Home, Tailscale, etc.)
  • Ideal for network labs and testing

docs.title: 4. Strong Community and Documentation
docs.text:
• Active GitHub repositories
  • Clear documentation and tutorials
  • Large user community
  • Frequent firmware updates

docs.title: Popular GL.iNet Products
docs.text:
Some well-known models include:

  • GL-MT3600BE (Beryl 7)
  • GL-MT3000 (Beryl AX) – Portable Wi-Fi 6 travel router
  • GL-MT1300 (Beryl) – Compact and powerful, great value
  • GL-AXT1800 (Slate AX) – High-performance travel router
  • GL-AR750S (Slate) – Classic dual-band travel router
  • GL-SFT1200 (Opal)
  • GL-AX1800 (Flint) – Home router with OpenWrt power
  • GL-MT6000 (Flint 2)

Each model targets a slightly different use case, from ultra-portable travel to full home routing.

docs.title: Who Is GL.iNet For?
docs.text:
GL.iNet is especially suitable for:

  • CS students learning networking
  • Developers needing flexible routing tools
  • Travelers who want secure internet access
  • Privacy-focused users
  • Homelab and self-hosting enthusiasts

If you enjoy tools like Linux, Docker, Tailscale, or OpenWrt, GL.iNet devices fit naturally into your workflow.

docs.title: Why People Choose GL.iNet
docs.text:
Compared to typical consumer routers, GL.iNet offers:

  • More control
  • Better VPN support
  • Smaller and more flexible hardware
  • Open-source friendliness
  • Fewer restrictions and vendor lock-in

It’s not just a router—it’s a networking toolkit.

docs.title: Final Thoughts
docs.text: GL.iNet has carved out a unique space in the networking world by focusing on power users without alienating beginners. Their devices strike a rare balance between simplicity and freedom, making them an excellent choice for anyone who wants to truly understand and control their network.
